policy: These are reading links, not imported textbook content. Author original explanations, examples, exercises, figures, and solutions for the app. External reading supplements the lesson and is not required for an app checkpoint to work.

primaryText.title: Algebra and Trigonometry 2e
primaryText.author: Jay Abramson and contributing authors
primaryText.access: Free web reading. The preface describes public answers for worked examples, Try It questions, and odd-numbered exercises; do not require instructor-only resources.
primaryText.reuse: The current preface displays CC BY-NC-SA terms. This plan links to pages and does not bundle book text or artwork. Recheck the applicable terms before any future reuse.

referenceSyntax: Each lesson reading identifies a source and section, for example os-3/3.4. The source link opens that chapter's outline, where the named section can be selected.

sources.label: Algebra foundations
sources.use: Optional bridges for arithmetic, notation, powers, radicals, expansion, factoring, and rational expressions.

sources.label: Equation methods
sources.use: Core equation work, complex-number basics, solution checks, and inequalities.

sources.label: Function concepts
sources.use: Functions, domains, graph behavior, compositions, transformations, and inverses.

sources.label: Linear models
sources.use: Slope, calibration, and model interpretation. Full regression is not required for this pack.

sources.label: Polynomial and rational behavior
sources.use: Polynomial structure, roots, rational graph behavior, radicals, and variation. The app must supply its own explicit sign-chart lesson.

sources.label: Exponential and logarithmic models
sources.use: Growth, decay, inverse operations, logarithm properties, solving equations, and model fitting.

sources.label: Angles and trigonometric ratios
sources.use: Angle measures, triangle ratios, unit-circle coordinates, and reciprocal/quotient functions.

sources.label: Periodic and inverse functions
sources.use: Periodic graphs, graph parameters, and principal-value inverse functions.

sources.label: Trigonometric reasoning
sources.use: Identities and equations. Half-angle, reduction, and product-to-sum material is optional beyond the specified core objectives.

sources.label: Triangle applications
sources.use: Only sections 10.1 and 10.2 are required here. Polar, vector, and parametric topics remain extension candidates for later packs.

sources.label: Systems and matrices
sources.use: Linear/nonlinear systems and matrix methods. Partial fractions in 11.4 are optional preparation for later calculus.

selectionRules: Assign sections by objective, not an entire textbook chapter by default. Mark optional sections explicitly.
Every external link needs a checked date, provider, purpose, access note, and an internal lesson alternative if the provider is unavailable.

Videos are optional enhancements. Add a video only after checking its complete topic coverage, captions, availability, and relevant start/end segment; no unreviewed video list is required for release.
External problem solutions should be used by learners only after an attempt. The app's own exercises must have complete original explanations and verifiable answer rules.
Reading links may need an internet connection. Built-in practice must not silently depend on an external calculator or a paid service.
